headline: Gas supply to improve within 5-7 days, says PM Tarique Rahman
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman announced that Bangladesh's gas supply is expected to improve within a week, attributing the current crisis to the Middle East war, illegal extraction, and past neglect of local exploration.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has stated that Bangladesh's gas supply situation is expected to improve significantly within the next five to seven days. He made these remarks on Friday while addressing the ongoing gas crisis at a program in the Dhaka-17 constituency.

During his speech, the Prime Minister acknowledged the challenges Bangladesh faces in electricity, gas, and fuel supplies, noting that the government has never denied the severity of the situation. He linked the energy crisis to the outbreak of the war in the Middle East, which began shortly after his government was formed, leading to a rise in international oil prices.

Tarique Rahman explained that the government initially tried to avoid raising oil prices to prevent additional public pressure. However, he stated that some dishonest individuals began misusing oil, forcing the government to increase prices to mitigate negative effects on the populace.

He also highlighted Bangladesh's reliance on imported gas due to declining pressure from locally produced gas and a prolonged period without new gas well drilling. A recent fire on one of the two ships stationed at sea for imported gas further disrupted supply, with the exact cause still under investigation.

The Prime Minister alleged that a dishonest group is illegally drawing gas from pipelines amid the ongoing shortage, using both foreign and locally made devices. While these activities benefit a few, they cause severe shortages for many other consumers in surrounding areas, a problem also observed in the electricity and fuel sectors.

Tarique Rahman criticized the previous 17 years for making the country's energy sector heavily dependent on foreign sources and for crippling Bapex, the state-owned oil and gas exploration company. He affirmed that his government has taken necessary steps to reactivate Bapex since assuming office.

He announced an initiative to explore 130 new gas wells, expressing hope for significant discoveries that will naturally improve the gas supply situation. The Prime Minister also urged citizens to actively participate in stopping illegal gas and electricity extraction, emphasizing that the country belongs to everyone and requires collective responsibility.

headline_marked: [[Tangail madrasa teacher sent to jail]] over alleged sexual assault of 10-year-old student
headline: Tangail madrasa teacher sent to jail over alleged sexual assault of 10-year-old student
summary: Police arrested the teacher after the victim's mother filed a case. The 10-year-old student was hospitalized, where doctors identified signs of alleged assault.
details: A Tangail court on Friday sent a madrasa teacher to jail for allegedly sexually assaulting his 10-year-old male student in Mirzapur upazila of Tangail.

Police arrested the teacher, identified as Al Amin, after the victim's mother filed a case against him with Mirzapur Police Station around noon on Friday. Abdullah Al Mamun, officer-in-charge of the police station, confirmed the arrest.
The accused was sent to jail through a Tangail court in the afternoon. Police officials stated they would file a remand prayer to question him further.
Citing the case statement, police reported that the boy was enrolled at the madrasa in January. He later fell ill and called his mother, asking her to take him home.

The boy was subsequently taken to Kumudini Hospital for treatment. There, a doctor informed the family that he had allegedly been sexually assaulted. The boy later told his family that Al Amin had allegedly been assaulting him for the last three months.
